FILED s517a (Opus, 2026-10-16) -- newly REACHED by #3262 (148 board rows:
Capture-Tiny capture_merged / tee_merged in 02 03 08 12).

    use Capture::Tiny qw(capture_merged);
    my $m = capture_merged { print "STDOUT:First line\nSecond line\n";
                             print STDERR "STDERR:First line\nSecond line\n" };
    perl 5.40.3: STDOUT lines first, then STDERR   (program order)
    PCL:         STDERR lines first, then STDOUT

scratch/s517a/pr/ct.pl.  Both handles are dup'ed onto ONE tmpfile; perl's
STDOUT reaches the file at its own flush, which Capture::Tiny forces before
STDERR is written (it turns autoflush on the captured handles); PCL's STDOUT
buffer is flushed only at the end.  Check $| / IO::Handle::autoflush on a
dup'ed STDOUT and the order of the two flushes in _open_std / the block run.


=== RE-SCOPED (s521b, 2026-10-18) ===
The 438 board rows blessed here were NOT the order: each is a separate like($got, qr/\Q$expected\E/) that failed on the \Q-newline
regex bug (#3510, fixed s521b) -- they LEFT the baseline by edit with #3510 / #3326.  What remains is the observation itself:
`capture_merged { print "STDOUT:1\n"; print STDERR "STDERR:1\n" }` is STDOUT-then-STDERR in perl, STDERR-first in PCL (probe
scratch/s521b/pr/ct1.pl, s521b tree).  No blessed row asserts it.  Not attempted in s521b (budget; member 4 was conditional).
subject: Capture::Tiny capture_merged / tee_merged: STDERR lands before STDOUT; perl keeps program order (148 board rows newly reached by #3262)
